The Nigeria Police Force has launched an investigation into a viral video showing armed police officers escorting businessman Linus Williams, popularly known as Blord. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, described the escort as “unlawful and illegal” in a statement posted on his official X account on Wednesday. Reacting to the video, he wrote, “Unlawful and illegal. Investigation has commenced into this incident please. We say #notoimpunity.” The video, posted by Blord on his Instagram page on Tuesday, shows him arriving at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport in Enugu. In the footage, Blord is seen in a black Cadillac bearing the personalised number plate “B-LORD”. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. The video also shows him walking alongside the officers at the airport and at other locations, including what appears to be his business premises. The officers are seen escorting him and opening the vehicle door for him. From the airport to a brief stop at BlordGroup Enugu branch, then back to Awka. Every move has its purpose, and the vision never takes a break. Blord is home!” In another post on his IG, the celebrity businessman said he was in Sabon Gari, Kano State, where he met his “brothers” before returning to Enugu. The development comes months after President Bola Tinubu ordered the withdrawal of police officers attached to Very Important Persons across the country and their redeployment to core policing duties. Tinubu issued the directive at a security meeting with service chiefs and the Director-General of the Department of State Services in Abuja on November 23, 2025. According to a statement by the President’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, VIPs requiring protection would be assigned armed operatives of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps instead of police officers. The President said the move was intended to strengthen police presence in communities, particularly those facing security challenges. On December 6, 2025, the police also deployed a Special Enforcement Team to monitor compliance with the directive, beginning with an operation in Lagos. The then Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Benjamin Hundeyin, said the exercise recorded no cases of unauthorised police escort deployment.
